html:
The Principality of Polotsk was a medieval East Slavic principality centred on the city of Polotsk on the Western Dvina, in what is now Belarus. It is on the map for 1100.

Polotsk grew up in the land of the Krivichs and is named in the Primary Chronicle under 862. In the late 900s its ruler Rogvolod was killed by Vladimir the Great, who took his daughter as wife. Their son's line kept Polotsk as its own, and it often defied the princes of Kyiv. Prince Vseslav even ruled Kyiv for a few months in 1068 and was remembered as a sorcerer.

Polotsk built its own Saint Sophia cathedral and traded down the Dvina to Riga. It later split into smaller principalities and around 1307 came under the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.
